name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district with long-serving incumbent Jim Clyburn
Clyburn's large cash advantage over a lightly funded challenger
No polls or expert ratings, but fundamentals strongly favor Democrats
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: Clyburn holds a D+13 seat with a big fundraising edge and no credible evidence of a competitive race; markets and fundamentals both point to a safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or major outside spending against Clyburn would warrant a relook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District is a heavily Democratic, majority-Black seat that Jim Clyburn has held for decades. He enters the general election with more than $1.6 million on hand after raising over $1.2 million, while Republican John Peterson reports no meaningful fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Clyburn's chances near 97 percent.

The district's partisan lean of roughly 13 points Democratic, combined with Clyburn's incumbency and financial dominance, makes an upset highly unlikely. The forecast expects Clyburn to win comfortably by a wide margin, consistent with recent cycles in this seat.
